mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar high-rate regimes (t-test p > 0.05), or the FEDFUNDS rate does not stay elevated for the required period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a concurrent drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market transition toward contraction, which precedes a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in one month while UNRATE decreases by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Over 30 such labor transition events, less than 40% result in negative 20-day SPX returns (Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer demand indicators (HOUST) exceed 1,500 thousand units for two consecutive months while industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat, it predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as market anticipates sustained economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 1500 for 2 consecutive months and INDPRO change < 0.5% in the same period
regime_hint: robust consumer demand with stable production
failure_condition: Across 50 such events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically higher than during neutral demand periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 10% in a month accompanied by a decline in consumer demand (GDPC1) of over 5% signals supply-side weakness that is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >10% in a month and GDPC1 decreases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: In 40 such contraction events, the 20-day SPX return is not significantly negative (Kolmogorov-Smirnov p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 200 for three consecutive months indicates deflationary pressure that tends to drive risk-on sentiment and a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: During 10 deflationary regimes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically higher than the average of non-deflationary regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in jobless claims (PAYEMS) without a corresponding decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a labor market shock that precedes a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% in a month while UNRATE remains flat or increases
failure_condition: In 25 such shock events, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (Kruskal-Wallis p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales proxy (not available in the given catalog; fallback to HOUST as demand proxy) above 1,400 units for three months predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates sustained demand strength.
failure_condition: During 15 such demand growth regimes, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand (GDPC1) by at least 5% in the same month indicates a dual supply-demand imbalance that is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >=5% and GDPC1 decreases by >=5% in the same month
regime_hint: dual contraction in supply and demand
failure_condition: Over 40 such events, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (Kolmogorov-Smirnov p > 0.10).
